facts.text: Tremé, founded in the 1810s, is one of New Orleans’ oldest neighborhoods and was originally the main area for free people of color.
The neighborhood’s name comes from Claude Tremé, who purchased the land in 1810, turning the former Morand Plantation into Faubourg Tremé.
Congo Square, now part of Louis Armstrong Park, was the historic gathering place where enslaved people danced and birthed early jazz rhythms.
Louis Armstrong Park honors the legendary trumpeter and preserves Congo Square, a site where slaves once made music every Sunday.
Tremé is home to the New Orleans African American Museum, which showcases the city’s black history and the African diaspora.
The neighborhood birthed the Rebirth Brass Band, with Joe’s Cozy Corner often cited as its birthplace, cementing Tremé’s brass band legacy.
